name: Grafana Loki
tagline: Label-indexed log aggregation: Prometheus-style streams, chunks on object storage, LogQL queries.
description: Grafana Loki stores logs as compressed chunks in object storage and indexes only a small set of labels per stream, the way Prometheus labels metrics. That makes ingestion and retention cheap compared with full-text indexes, at the price of brute-force scanning for content filters, which Loki parallelises across queriers. LogQL combines label selectors, line filters, parsers and metric aggregations, and Grafana, Alloy and OpenTelemetry are first-class clients. The 3.x releases added structured metadata, native OTLP ingestion and bloom-filter acceleration to ease high-cardinality fields, but label design is still the biggest operational decision.

pricing.notes: Free to self-host; Grafana Cloud Logs has a free tier; Grafana Enterprise Logs is contract-priced.

scale.notes: Monolithic, simple-scalable and microservices modes; chunks and TSDB index live in object storage.

strengths: Cheap to run: small label index and compressed chunks on object storage
LogQL feels familiar to PromQL users and can turn logs into metrics
Tight integration with Grafana, Mimir and Tempo for metrics-logs-traces correlation
Native OTLP ingestion and structured metadata for OpenTelemetry pipelines
Official Kubernetes operator and Helm charts
weaknesses: Content searches scan data, so needle-in-haystack queries over long ranges are slow
High-cardinality labels break performance; label design needs discipline
Microservices mode has many components and tuning knobs
useCases: Kubernetes and application logs alongside Prometheus
Deriving metrics and alerts from log lines
Correlating logs with traces in Grafana
notIdealFor: Security analytics needing fast arbitrary-field search
